notes: DJI Transmission (Standard Combo) is a two-piece wireless video transmission system: a DJI Video Transmitter (TX) and DJI Video Receiver (RX), linked over DJI O3 Pro wireless (2.4/5.8GHz + DFS, up to 6km FCC / 4km CE, 40Mbps max bitrate, 1080p60 max, ~70ms latency). Ports above are split by unit (TX:/RX: prefixes) since they are separate physical boxes, not one chassis. Both TX and RX are identical in size/weight (approx. 350g each, 127x87x26mm excl. antennas) and each has 2 detachable RF antenna connectors (proprietary, not in the standard connector taxonomy, so omitted as ports) plus a proprietary battery-sled "External Power Input Port" for WB37 or NP-F batteries (also omitted, not a standard connector type). Port existence/direction/count is sourced directly from DJI's own official User Guides (DJI_Video_Transmitter_User_Guide_v1.2.pdf and DJI_Video_Receiver_User_Guide_v1.0.pdf, linked from the dji.com/transmission/downloads page) which is why direction/topology confidence is high; however neither manual states SDI or HDMI version numbers, so the sdi-3g and hdmi-1.4 grades are inferred from secondary retailer/press sources (B&H product listing, newsshooter.com hands-on) describing "dual 3G-SDI Output Ports" and an "HDMI 1.4 Type-A Output Port" on the receiver — hence overall confidence is medium. DC power connectors on both units are locking round connectors (compatible with P-TAP/Ronin 2 accessory power via adapter cables), approximated here as dc-barrel since no closer match exists in the connector list. Not modeled: the alternative "DJI Transmission (High-Bright Monitor Combo)" variant, which pairs the same TX with a DJI High-Bright Remote Monitor (an integrated monitor+receiver with its own separate HDMI-out-only expansion plate) instead of the standalone Video Receiver.
